title: A SARIF 2.1.0 log, regenerated from the project's own static analysis before the gate reads it

rows.citable: file:reports/scan.sarif#the-rule-id — the scan must know the rule and record no open finding

removes: the machine, account, process id and environment of each invocation
the working directory's absolute path in every string, each artifactLocation uri made relative with / separators
normalisation.keeps: every run, tool, rule in force, result, level, message and location, as the tool wrote them

github.pin: a 40-character commit of stranxik/runward that carries this file, never a branch or a tag

gitlab.include: include: project: (a project of yours the agent cannot write, holding this file), ref: (a 40-character commit of it), file: (this template); or include: remote: (this file at a stranxik/runward commit) with integrity: (its sha256)

runwardRun.onTheSamplePolicy: a leg runward-run accepts, run in an image that carries this package at /opt/runward-integrations; the sample policy's own lint leg runs the example's lint-committable.mjs instead, a script in the judged tree that writes the same log, on the stock Node.js image

control.fixture: the shipped example, written by runward init --example with the runward under test, with the example's lockfile

sabotage.summary: a bearer token written as a literal in a new adapter that no row cites, a shape the built-in analyzers do not know and the example's lint configuration refuses; the committed SARIF log still records no result

doesNotCatch.why: the guard's change breaks a test, not a lint rule: the regenerated log records no result, as the committed one
the tests and the journal changed within what the lint configuration allows: the regenerated log records no result

limits: A log says what its rules saw: a credential in a shape the configuration does not list, or a finding of a rule no row cites, refuses nothing.
The configuration is the project's: a rule switched off disappears from the log, and a row citing it is then refused as absent, never as clean; a rule loosened in its options is not seen.
For a project linted by ESLint the recipe writes the log itself (src/tools/eslint-sarif.mjs); a tool that writes SARIF on its own is run as the project runs it, and only normalised.
As a plain CI step its report is declared: nothing binds it to the tree after the run.
